story.conflict: The birthday girl pressures the narrator to split an expensive dinner equally even though several guests ordered far less, then publicly calls her cheap when she asks to pay only for what she ordered.
story.hook: My friend called me cheap for refusing to split her birthday dinner evenly, then the waiter showed me the bill she didn't want us to see.
story.premise: A woman refuses to pay an inflated equal-share bill at her friend's birthday dinner and discovers the birthday girl quietly included the price of a complimentary champagne bottle so she could collect extra money from everyone.
story.punchline: You charged us for a bottle the restaurant gave you for free.
story.script:
There were eight of us at dinner, and before we even sat down, my friend Jenna announced that nobody was allowed to argue about the bill because it was her birthday and she wanted a stress-free night. Fine. I ordered pasta, one mocktail, and dessert. Two other people ordered about the same. Jenna and her closest friends went big: steaks, seafood, cocktails, appetizers for the table, and a bottle of champagne that cost more than my entire meal.

At the end, Jenna grabbed the bill before anyone else could see it. She tapped on her calculator for maybe ten seconds and announced that everyone owed one hundred and forty-eight dollars. I actually laughed because I thought she was joking. My food was barely sixty. When I asked if we could just pay for what we ordered, she rolled her eyes and said, 'Seriously? It's my birthday. Don't make this awkward.'

Then she said it louder so the whole table could hear: 'If money is that tight, you could've stayed home.'

That annoyed me enough to stop being polite. I asked to see the receipt. Jenna folded it in half and said she'd already calculated everything. One of our friends offered to send me a photo, but Jenna immediately slid the bill under her handbag. That was when I knew this wasn't really about convenience.

I went to the restroom, and on the way back I quietly asked our waiter whether the restaurant could print me an itemized copy so I could reimburse Jenna correctly. He looked confused and said, 'Reimburse her for what? The card hasn't been charged yet.'

Then he printed the current bill. The total was much lower than the number Jenna had used. The champagne bottle was listed, then completely removed. Earlier in the night, our appetizers had arrived almost forty minutes late, and the manager had comped the bottle as an apology. Jenna knew that. She had thanked him.

I brought the copy back to the table and asked Jenna to explain the math. She tried to say taxes and tip made up the difference, but even with a generous tip, the numbers were nowhere close. So I pointed at the zeroed-out champagne line and said, 'You charged us for a bottle the restaurant gave you for free.'

The table went silent. One friend pulled out her phone and recalculated everything. Jenna had been asking for almost two hundred dollars more than the actual bill. Suddenly the people who had called me difficult wanted their own itemized totals too.

I paid for my meal, added a good tip, and left. Jenna didn't get a stress-free birthday dinner after all, but she did get exactly the kind of split bill she deserved: everyone paid for themselves.
story.twist: The restaurant had removed the champagne charge and comped the bottle after a service issue, but the birthday girl still included its full price in the amount she collected from the group.

youtube.description: My friend called me cheap for refusing an equal split at her birthday dinner. Then the waiter printed the itemized bill she had hidden, and one comped bottle exposed the whole thing. #WackyDramas #Storytime #Drama #Friends
youtube.title: She Tried to Profit From Her Own Birthday Dinner
